examples.ko: 우리 동네 근처에 쓰레기 매립장 공사가 시작됐어요.
examples.en: Construction of a landfill has started near our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 매립장이 가득 차서 새 부지를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The landfill is full, so they are looking for a new site.
Residents are having a hard time because of the smell from the landfill.

examples.ko: 쓰레기를 줄여야 매립장을 오래 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: We have to reduce waste to keep using the landfill longer.

examples.ko: 매립장으로 가는 트럭이 하루에도 수십 대예요.
examples.en: Dozens of trucks head to the landfill every day.

examples.ko: 이 매립장은 곧 공원으로 바뀔 예정이에요.
examples.en: This landfill is scheduled to be turned into a park soon.

explain: '쓰레기 매립장'으로 자주 써요. 쓰레기를 태우는 '소각장'과 짝으로 뉴스에 많이 나와요. 새로 짓는 문제로 주민과 갈등이 생기는 기사도 많아요.

phrases.en: The garbage landfill is far from the city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔하게 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation.

phrases.example: 새 매립장 부지가 아직 정해지지 않았어요.
phrases.en: The site for the new landfill hasn't been decided yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 매립장을 지을 땅을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the land where a landfill will be built.

phrases.example: 몇 년 안에 매립장이 가득 찰 거예요.
phrases.en: The landfill will be full within a few years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓰레기 처리 문제가 심각하다는 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in news about waste disposal problems.

explain_en: It is often used as '쓰레기 매립장'. It frequently appears in the news paired with '소각장' (incineration plant). There are also many articles about conflicts with residents over building a new one.

examples.ko: 저는 주말마다 문화원에서 한국어 수업을 들어요.
examples.en: Every weekend I take a Korean class at the cultural center.
There is a Korean cultural center in this city.
The cultural center held a hanbok experience event.
I decided to meet a friend in front of the cultural center.
The cultural center is closed on Mondays.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 문화원에서 무료 전시를 해요.
examples.en: The cultural center in my neighborhood has a free exhibition.

explain: '문화원'은 한 나라의 문화를 소개하고 강좌나 전시를 여는 기관이에요. 외국에 있는 '한국문화원', 한국 안의 '지역 문화원'처럼 앞에 이름을 붙여서 말해요.

phrases.en: I visited the Korean Cultural Center in Paris.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외국에서 한국 문화를 소개하는 기관 이름으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used as the name of an institute introducing Korean culture abroad.

phrases.example: 우리 동네 지역 문화원에서 무료 강좌를 열어요.
phrases.en: The local cultural center in my neighborhood holds free classes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 지역의 문화 활동을 돕는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A place that supports cultural activities in one area.

phrases.en: I'm learning calligraphy in a cultural center class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문화원에서 여는 수업을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to classes offered at a cultural center.

explain_en: 문화원 is an institution that introduces a country's culture through classes and exhibitions. People attach a name in front, as in '한국문화원' abroad or a local 문화원 within Korea.

en: to be crowded; to be concentrated

examples.en: Tourists are concentrated in the city center.

examples.ko: 병원이 한 건물에 밀집돼서 찾기 쉬워요.
examples.en: Clinics are grouped in one building, so they are easy to find.
On weekends, people crowd into the park.

examples.ko: 대학교 근처에 원룸이 밀집된 동네가 있어요.
examples.en: Near the university there is a neighborhood packed with studio apartments.

examples.ko: 학원이 밀집되어 있는 거리에는 학생이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many students on streets where academies are clustered.
The more the population concentrates, the more housing prices rise.

explain: '밀집하다'는 스스로 모여 있는 모습을, '밀집되다'는 어떤 이유로 한곳에 모이게 된 결과를 말하는 느낌이에요. 실제 말에서는 두 표현이 거의 바꿔 쓰여요. 보통 '~에 밀집돼 있다'로 많이 써요.

phrases.en: It's an alley where restaurants are packed together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙여 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used before a noun.

phrases.en: Shops are clustered near the station.
phrases.nuance_ko: '밀집돼 있다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly interchangeable with 밀집돼 있다.

phrases.en: People are gathered in the square.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한곳에 많이 모여 있을 때 일상에서 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday way to say many are gathered in one place.

explain_en: 밀집하다 describes things gathering on their own, while 밀집되다 describes the result of being gathered somewhere for some reason. In practice the two swap freely. It is usually used as ~에 밀집돼 있다.

t90.ax: On weekends, people crowd into the park.

en: to be crowded; to be concentrated

examples.ko: 이 동네에는 작은 가게가 밀집해 있어요.
examples.en: Small shops are densely packed in this neighborhood.
People were crowded in one place, so it was hard to walk.
Parking is hard in areas packed with apartments.
Passengers pack the subway during rush hour.

examples.ko: 공장이 밀집하는 곳은 공기가 안 좋아요.
examples.en: The air is bad where factories are concentrated.
The more densely buildings are packed, the more dangerous a fire is.

explain: '모이다'와 달리 '밀집하다'는 좁은 곳에 아주 촘촘하게 몰려 있다는 느낌이에요. 사람, 가게, 건물, 공장처럼 눈에 보이는 것에 쓰고, '밀집 지역'으로도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: This is a densely packed area full of restaurants.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무언가가 촘촘하게 모인 곳을 한 단어처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names an area where something is tightly clustered, as a single compound.

phrases.en: I grew up in a neighborhood crowded with small houses.
phrases.nuance_ko: '밀집하다'를 '-ㄴ' 형태로 바꿔 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, used to describe the noun that follows.

phrases.en: People are crowded in front of the exit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '밀집해 있다'보다 쉬운 말이고, 한곳으로 모인 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word than 밀집해 있다 for people gathered in one spot.

explain_en: Unlike '모이다' (to gather), '밀집하다' gives the feel of being packed tightly into a small space. It is used for visible things like people, shops, buildings and factories, and the phrase '밀집 지역' (densely packed area) is common.

t90.ax: Passengers pack the subway during rush hour.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 전국 방방곡곡에 울려 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: This song rang out in every corner of the country.
The rumor spread to every corner of the land.
My dream is to travel to every corner of Korea.
People cheering from all over the country gathered.
It is a show that goes around finding good restaurants in every corner of the country.

examples.ko: 방방곡곡의 시장마다 특색 있는 음식이 있어요.
examples.en: Every market in every corner of the country has its own special food.

explain: '전국 방방곡곡', '우리나라 방방곡곡'처럼 한 곳도 빠짐없이 모든 곳을 강조할 때 써요. 그냥 '전국'보다 구석구석까지라는 느낌이 있고, '곳곳'과 비슷해요. 뒤에 에/에서/을 등이 붙어요.

phrases.en: I traveled all over the country looking for good restaurants.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전국'과 함께 써서 나라 전체를 구석구석 강조하는 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, stressing every corner of the whole country.

phrases.en: People gathered from every corner of the country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에서'를 붙이면 어디에서 오는지, 어디에서 일어나는지를 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle 에서, it says where people come from or where something happens.

phrases.en: Flowers have bloomed all around the city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방방곡곡보다 쉽고 일상적이며, 넓은 지역뿐 아니라 작은 장소에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more casual than 방방곡곡, and works for small places as well as large areas.

explain_en: It is used in phrases like '전국 방방곡곡' and '우리나라 방방곡곡' to stress every place without leaving one out. Compared with plain '전국', it feels like reaching every nook and cranny, and it is close to '곳곳'. Particles like 에, 에서 and 을 attach to it.

examples.en: This village is on the edge of the country.
In the old days, soldiers guarded the frontier.

examples.ko: 변방 지역은 교통이 불편한 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Remote border regions often have poor transportation.

examples.ko: 그는 문화의 변방에서 새로운 것을 만들었어요.
examples.en: He created something new on the fringes of culture.

examples.ko: 변방의 작은 학교가 전국 대회에서 우승했어요.
examples.en: A small school from a remote area won the national competition.
I feel like I keep getting pushed out to the margins.

explain: 나라의 가장자리뿐 아니라 '중심에서 먼 곳, 주목받지 못하는 분야'를 비유할 때도 써요. 반대말은 '중심'이나 '중앙'이고, 일상에서는 '외진 곳'이라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: Remote areas also need schools and hospitals.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중심에서 멀리 떨어진 지역을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to areas far from the center.

phrases.example: 그 분야는 한동안 변방으로 밀려나 있었어요.
phrases.en: That field was pushed to the margins for a while.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중요한 자리에서 멀어져 주목받지 못하게 되었다는 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Figuratively means being pushed away from the spotlight.
phrases.en_equiv: to be pushed to the margins

phrases.example: 할머니 집은 버스도 잘 안 오는 외진 곳에 있어요.
phrases.en: Grandma's house is in a remote place where the bus hardly ever comes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '변방' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday word to use instead of 변방.

explain_en: Besides the edge of a country, it is used figuratively for a place far from the center or a field that gets little attention. Its opposites are '중심' and '중앙', and in daily talk people also say '외진 곳'.

examples.ko: 이 호텔은 부대시설이 아주 잘 되어 있어요.
examples.en: This hotel has very good additional facilities.

examples.ko: 수영장과 헬스장 같은 부대시설을 무료로 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can use extra facilities like the pool and gym for free.

examples.ko: 아파트를 고를 때 부대시설도 꼭 확인해요.
examples.en: When I choose an apartment, I always check the extra facilities too.
The campsite's extra facilities include a shower room and a small shop.

examples.ko: 공원 부대시설의 안전 점검이 다음 주에 있어요.
examples.en: The safety inspection of the park's extra facilities is next week.
We don't charge separately for using the extra facilities.

explain: 호텔, 아파트, 학교 같은 주요 건물에 딸려 있는 수영장, 주차장, 매점 같은 시설을 말할 때 써요. 숙소나 부동산 광고에서 자주 보이고, 비슷한 말로 '편의시설'도 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 이 아파트 근처에는 편의시설이 많아서 살기 편해요.
phrases.en: There are many convenient facilities near this apartment, so it's comfortable to live in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부대시설과 비슷하지만, 사람들이 편하게 쓰는 시설이라는 점을 더 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 부대시설, but it puts more emphasis on facilities that make life convenient.

phrases.example: 새로 지은 리조트는 부대시설이 잘 되어 있어요.
phrases.en: The newly built resort has well-equipped additional facilities.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숙소나 건물을 소개할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation when describing a hotel or building.

phrases.example: 호텔 손님은 부대시설을 이용할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Hotel guests can use the additional facilities.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수영장이나 헬스장 같은 시설을 쓴다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when saying you use facilities such as the pool or gym.

explain_en: It is used for facilities attached to a main building such as a hotel, apartment or school, like a pool, parking lot or shop. You often see it in accommodation and real-estate ads. '편의시설' is a similar word that is also common.

en: to be scattered; to be dotted; to be sparse

examples.ko: 작은 섬들이 바다 위에 산재해 있어요.
examples.en: Small islands are scattered across the sea.

examples.ko: 공원에는 쓰레기가 산재해서 보기 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Trash is strewn around the park, so it looks bad.

examples.ko: 이 지역에는 오래된 절이 곳곳에 산재해요.
examples.en: Old temples are scattered throughout this region.

examples.ko: 문제가 산재한 회사라서 고칠 게 많아요.
examples.en: The company has problems all over, so there is a lot to fix.

examples.ko: 자료가 여러 파일에 산재할 때는 정리가 필요해요.
examples.en: When data is scattered across many files, it needs to be organized.
Toys were scattered all over the child's room.

explain: '산재하다'는 물건·건물·문제가 여기저기 흩어져 있을 때 써요. 보통 '산재해 있다' 모양으로 말해요. 한곳에 모여 있으면 '밀집하다'를 쓰고, 일상에서는 '흩어져 있다'가 더 쉬워요.

phrases.en: Empty houses are scattered all over the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: '산재하다'를 가장 자연스럽게 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most natural way to use '산재하다'.

phrases.en: Toys are scattered on the bedroom floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 일상 대화에서 더 쉽고 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It has the same meaning but is easier and more common in everyday talk.

phrases.example: 회사에 산재한 문제를 하나씩 풀어 가요.
phrases.en: We solve the many scattered problems in the company one by one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 쓰는 모양으로, 문제가 여기저기 많을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This modifier form describes problems that exist in many different places.

explain_en: 산재하다 is for objects, buildings, or problems spread out here and there. It usually appears as 산재해 있다. Things packed in one place are 밀집하다, and in daily talk 흩어져 있다 is easier.

t90.ax: Small islands are scattered across the sea.

examples.en: The wind blows in from the southwest.
The southwestern region of Korea is famous for rice.
Keep going toward the southwest.
There are many islands along the southwest coast.
The sun is sinking toward the southwest.
My house is southwest of the school.

explain: 서남과 남서는 같은 방향이에요. 일기예보에서는 '남서풍'처럼 남서를 쓰고, 지역 이름에는 '서남해안'처럼 서남이 보여요. 같은 짝으로 동남과 남동이 있어요.

phrases.en: The southwest sky turned red.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쪽'을 붙이면 방향을 가리키는 말이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 쪽 makes it a direction word.

phrases.en: It rains a lot in the southwest region.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라나 도시의 한 부분을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name a part of a country or city.

phrases.en: If you go southwest, you reach the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서남'과 같은 방향이고 일기예보에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same direction as 서남; more common in weather reports.

explain_en: 서남 and 남서 point to the same direction. Weather forecasts say 남서풍, while 서남 shows up in place names like 서남해안. 동남 and 남동 form a similar pair.

examples.ko: 올림픽 선수촌에는 식당과 체육관이 다 있어요.
examples.en: The Olympic athletes' village has a cafeteria and a gym.
National team athletes train together at the athletes' village.

examples.ko: 선수촌 안에서 여러 나라 선수들이 인사를 나눴어요.
examples.en: Athletes from different countries greeted one another inside the village.

examples.ko: 어제 텔레비전에서 선수촌 안을 소개하는 방송을 봤어요.
examples.en: Yesterday I watched a TV show introducing the inside of the athletes' village.
My younger sibling was selected as a representative and entered the athletes' village.

examples.ko: 선수촌 식당 음식이 맛있다는 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard that the food at the athletes' village cafeteria is good.

explain: 올림픽이나 아시안게임 때 선수들이 머무는 마을도 선수촌이고, 국가대표가 모여서 훈련하는 시설도 선수촌이라고 불러요. 어느 쪽인지는 앞뒤 이야기로 알 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 올림픽 선수촌에서 여러 나라 선수를 만났어요.
phrases.en: I met athletes from many countries in the Olympic village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대회 기간 동안 선수들이 머무는 마을을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the village where athletes stay during the Games.

phrases.en: The national team players entered the training center.
phrases.nuance_ko: 훈련이나 대회를 위해 선수촌에서 지내기 시작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when athletes begin staying there for training or a competition.

phrases.en: While I stayed at the training center, I trained every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에서 지내다'를 붙여 머무는 생활을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '에서 지내다' describes living there.

explain_en: The village where athletes stay during the Olympics or Asian Games is called a '선수촌', and so is the facility where national team members gather to train. The context tells you which one is meant.

examples.en: A military transport plane left carrying relief supplies.

examples.ko: 대형 수송기는 한 번에 많은 짐을 옮길 수 있어요.
examples.en: A large cargo plane can carry a lot of goods at once.

examples.ko: 수송기가 공항에 도착해서 짐을 내리고 있어요.
examples.en: The cargo plane has arrived at the airport and is unloading.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 수송기 사진을 봤는데 정말 커요.
examples.en: I saw a photo of a transport plane on the news, and it's really big.

examples.ko: 홍수 지역으로 가는 수송기에 의료진도 탔어요.
examples.en: Medical staff also boarded the transport plane heading to the flood area.
Transport planes and passenger planes are used very differently.

explain: 사람을 태우는 '여객기'와 달리 짐이나 장비를 나르는 비행기예요. 뉴스에서는 군 장비나 구호물자를 옮기는 이야기에서 자주 들을 수 있어요. 짐만 나르는 민간 비행기는 '화물기'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: They carried the relief supplies by transport plane.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짐을 비행기로 나른다는 뜻을 분명히 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes clear that goods are carried by air.

phrases.en: The transport plane landed safely on the runway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 수송기 이야기를 할 때 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often heard in news about transport planes.

phrases.en: The cargo plane arrived at Incheon Airport at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짐만 나르는 민간 비행기는 '화물기'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A civilian plane that carries only freight is called '화물기'.

explain_en: Unlike a '여객기' (passenger plane), this carries goods and equipment. You often hear it in news about military gear or relief supplies. A civilian plane that only carries freight is also called a '화물기'.

examples.en: My older brother rides a scooter to work.

examples.ko: 제주도에서 스쿠터를 빌려서 한 바퀴 돌았어요.
examples.en: I rented a scooter in Jeju and rode all the way around.
A scooter is smaller and lighter than a motorcycle.

examples.ko: 비가 오는 날에는 스쿠터를 타기 무서워요.
examples.en: I am scared to ride a scooter on rainy days.
A delivery scooter went through the alley.

examples.ko: 스쿠터를 탈 때는 헬멧을 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: You must wear a helmet when riding a scooter.

explain: 스쿠터는 바퀴가 작고 발을 올리는 판이 있는 가벼운 오토바이예요. 한국에서는 '오토바이'가 더 넓은 말이라 스쿠터도 오토바이에 들어가요. 아이들이 발로 차며 타는 것은 '킥보드'라고 불러서 서로 달라요.

phrases.en: I ride a scooter with my friend on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스쿠터를 탈 때 가장 기본으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to say you ride a scooter.

phrases.en: I'm going to rent a scooter at the travel destination.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여행지에서 잠깐 빌려 탈 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for renting one briefly while traveling.

phrases.en: There are more electric scooters these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기름 대신 전기로 가는 스쿠터를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a scooter that runs on electricity instead of gasoline.

explain_en: A 스쿠터 is a light motorbike with small wheels and a flat footboard. In Korea '오토바이' is the wider word, so a scooter counts as one too. The kind kids push with a foot is called '킥보드', which is different.

examples.en: Seoul is the heart of Korea's politics and economy.
There is a big square at the heart of the city.
A spy got into the very core of the company.

examples.ko: 그 숲의 심장부에는 오래된 나무가 서 있어요.
examples.en: An old tree stands at the heart of that forest.
The engine is the heart of the machine.
This place is called the heart of the culture industry.

explain: 몸의 '심장'보다 '가장 중요한 중심 부분'을 비유할 때가 대부분이에요. 도시, 조직, 기계, 숲의 한가운데에 쓰고 '중심부'보다 힘이 모인 곳이라는 느낌이 더 강해요. 실제 심장의 위치는 보통 '심장'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Reporters covered the heart of power.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정치나 조직의 가장 중요한 중심을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the most important center of politics or an organization.

phrases.en: There are many tall buildings in the city center.
phrases.nuance_ko: '심장부'보다 힘이 모인 느낌은 약하고 단순히 가운데 부분을 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Weaker than 심장부 in terms of power; it just means the central part.

phrases.en: The train passes through the heart of the city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도시나 지역의 한가운데를 지난다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means passing through the very center of a city or region.

explain_en: It is used far more often as a metaphor for the most important central part than for the body's '심장'. It applies to the middle of a city, organization, machine or forest, and feels stronger than '중심부', as the place where power gathers. The actual organ is usually just '심장'.

dis.h: center or core of a city or organization
gh: feelings or mind inside a person

p.n: 심장 is a more figurative 'heart'; 심장부 is the central area.

t90.ax: The engine is the heart of the machine.

examples.ko: 황 영감네 안마당이 바로 눈앞에 보여요.
examples.en: I can see old Mr. Hwang's inner yard right in front of me.

examples.ko: 할머니 댁 안마당에는 감나무가 한 그루 있어요.
examples.en: There is a persimmon tree in my grandmother's courtyard.
The kids are playing, kicking a ball in the courtyard.
I hung the laundry out in the courtyard.
In a hanok, you reach the inner courtyard once you pass the gate.
After sweeping the courtyard, I felt refreshed.

explain: 대문 안쪽, 집 가운데나 안쪽에 있는 마당이에요. '앞마당', '뒷마당'처럼 집에서 마당의 위치에 따라 이름이 달라요. 한옥이나 시골집 이야기에서 나와요.

phrases.en: The children play ball in the courtyard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에서'를 붙여 어디에서 하는 일인지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle '-eseo' to say where something happens.

phrases.en: I like this house because the courtyard is wide.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마당의 크기를 설명할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the size of the yard.

phrases.en: Every morning my grandmother sweeps the courtyard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시골집이나 한옥에서 자주 보는 일상 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common everyday scene at a rural or traditional house.

explain_en: It is the yard inside the gate, in the middle or inner part of a house. Like '앞마당' and '뒷마당', the name depends on where the yard is relative to the house. It shows up in talk about hanok and country houses.

examples.en: Small houses are huddled neatly together.

examples.ko: 하천 건너편은 오밀조밀 붙은 지붕들이 마치 장난감 마을 같았어요.
examples.en: The other side of the stream, with its snugly packed roofs, looked like a toy village.
Shops are packed closely along the alley.

examples.ko: 책상 위에 소품을 오밀조밀 꾸며 놓았어요.
examples.en: I arranged small items neatly on my desk.

examples.ko: 과일이 상자 안에 오밀조밀 담겨 있어요.
examples.en: The fruit is packed snugly in the box.

examples.ko: 동네가 오밀조밀 붙어 있어서 걸어 다니기 좋아요.
examples.en: The neighborhood is compact, so it's nice to get around on foot.

explain: 작은 것들이 촘촘하고 아기자기하게 모여 있는 모습에 써요. 답답하다기보다 정돈되고 귀여운 느낌으로 말할 때가 많아요.

phrases.example: 그림 속에 작은 집들이 오밀조밀 모여 있어요.
phrases.en: Small houses are clustered neatly together in the picture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 것들이 가깝게 모여 있는 모습에 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use, for small things gathered closely.

phrases.example: 책상 위에 작은 소품이 오밀조밀 놓여 있어요.
phrases.en: Small items are arranged neatly on the desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 촘촘하지만 보기 좋게 놓인 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For items placed close together yet pleasantly arranged.

phrases.en: Little shops stand packed side by side.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물이나 가게가 서로 바짝 붙은 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For buildings or shops standing right next to each other.

explain_en: It describes small things gathered closely in a neat, charming way. It often feels tidy and cute rather than stuffy.
